start_codegen_session.rationale: Starts a local code generation session (`Start a new code generation session`) and takes an `outputPath` for later generated tests, but does not advertise returning page data or sending data to an attacker-readable destination.

end_codegen_session.rationale: Ends a session and writes a generated test file (`generate the test file`) identified by `sessionId`; the advertised text does not say it returns the generated file content or sends it off-host.

get_codegen_session.rationale: It returns information about a recorded session (`Get information about a code generation session`). Such a session records Playwright actions (`record Playwright actions`), which may include non-public user-entered data and attacker-controlled page/action details. Result contents are not specified, so this is treated as potentially returning both secret and untrusted session data.

clear_codegen_session.rationale: Clears local session state (`Clear a code generation session`) selected by `sessionId`; no returned external content or attacker-readable delivery is advertised.

playwright_navigate.rationale: Navigates to an agent-supplied `url` (`Navigate to a URL`), causing a request to an agent-chosen URL/host, which is a sink. It does not advertise returning the page body itself.

playwright_screenshot.rationale: Returns/captures a screenshot of the current page (`Take a screenshot of the current page or a specific element`), which can include non-public authenticated/local content or attacker-controlled page content. It can also save a PNG file (`Save screenshot as PNG file`).

playwright_click.rationale: Clicking page elements (`Click an element on the page`) can submit or trigger browser requests from the current page, including sending values previously supplied by the agent to an attacker-controlled page.

playwright_iframe_click.rationale: Clicking an element in an iframe (`Click an element in an iframe on the page`) can submit or trigger requests from attacker-controlled iframe/page content carrying agent-supplied page state.

playwright_iframe_fill.rationale: Fills an iframe element with an agent-supplied `value` (`Value to fill`); attacker-controlled page/iframe scripts or later submission can read that value.

playwright_fill.rationale: Fills an input field (`fill out an input field`) with an agent-supplied `value`; on an attacker-controlled page this delivers the value to attacker-readable script or later form submission.

playwright_select.rationale: Selects a value in a page `<select>` (`Value to select`), making agent-supplied data observable to the current page and possible later submission.

playwright_hover.rationale: Only hovers an element (`Hover an element on the page`). It can change page state, but the advertised input does not carry substantive agent data to an attacker-readable destination and no returned content is advertised.

playwright_upload_file.rationale: Uploads a host file selected by `filePath` (`Absolute path to the file to upload`) into the current page (`Upload a file to an input[type='file'] element`), which can send that file to an attacker-controlled page/site.

playwright_evaluate.rationale: Executes arbitrary browser-page JavaScript (`Execute JavaScript in the browser console`). The script can read and return current page data, including non-public authenticated/local page data or attacker-authored content, and can send agent-supplied data via browser requests from the page context. This is browser execution, not advertised host code execution.

playwright_console_logs.rationale: Retrieves browser console logs (`Retrieve console logs from the browser`), which may contain secrets logged by authenticated/local pages or attacker-authored log text from attacker pages. It can also clear logs (`clear logs after retrieval`).

playwright_resize.rationale: Resizes/reconfigures viewport and device emulation (`Resize the browser viewport`, `device presets`). It changes browser state but does not advertise returning outside content or sending agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

playwright_close.rationale: Closes local browser resources (`Close the browser and release all resources`) without returning outside content or delivering data externally.

playwright_get.rationale: Performs an HTTP GET to an agent-supplied `url` (`URL to perform GET operation`), so it is a request to an agent-chosen host. The response can be attacker-controlled or non-public if the URL reaches localhost/intranet/authenticated resources or uses supplied authorization (`Bearer token`).

playwright_post.rationale: Posts agent-supplied body data (`Data to post in the body`) to an agent-supplied `url` (`URL to perform POST operation`), an attacker-readable sink. The HTTP response may be attacker-controlled or non-public depending on the target and authorization.

playwright_put.rationale: Sends agent-supplied body data (`Data to PUT in the body`) to an agent-supplied `url` (`URL to perform PUT operation`), an attacker-readable sink. The response can be attacker-controlled or non-public.

playwright_patch.rationale: Sends agent-supplied body data (`Data to PATCH in the body`) to an agent-supplied `url` (`URL to perform PATCH operation`), an attacker-readable sink. The response can be attacker-controlled or non-public.

playwright_delete.rationale: Performs an HTTP DELETE to an agent-supplied `url` (`URL to perform DELETE operation`), which is a request to an agent-chosen host and may change server state. The response can be attacker-controlled or non-public.

playwright_expect_response.rationale: Only starts a local wait operation for a matching response (`start waiting for a HTTP response`, `does not wait for its completion`) using an identifier and URL pattern; it does not advertise returning response content or contacting a new URL.

playwright_assert_response.rationale: Waits for and validates a previously observed HTTP response and may inspect the `response body` (`Data to expect in the body of the HTTP response`). The text does not specify whether the body is returned, so under the least restrictive reading it may expose non-public or attacker-controlled response content.

playwright_custom_user_agent.rationale: Sets an agent-supplied user agent (`Custom User Agent`) that will be sent by the browser to subsequently visited sites, including attacker-controlled ones.

playwright_get_visible_text.rationale: Returns visible text of the current page (`Get the visible text content of the current page`), which may be authenticated/local secret content or attacker-authored web content.

playwright_get_visible_html.rationale: Returns HTML from the current page (`Get the HTML content of the current page`), which may contain non-public authenticated/local data or attacker-authored markup. Options only clean/filter the returned HTML.

playwright_go_back.rationale: Navigates within existing browser history (`Navigate back in browser history`). It changes browser state, but has no agent-chosen URL argument and does not advertise returning page content.

playwright_go_forward.rationale: Navigates within existing browser history (`Navigate forward in browser history`). It changes browser state, but has no agent-chosen URL argument and does not advertise returning page content.

playwright_drag.rationale: Drags an element to a target (`Drag an element to a target location`), changing page state. The advertised inputs are selectors, with no substantive content value and no returned outside content.

playwright_press_key.rationale: Presses an agent-specified key (`Press a keyboard key`) optionally after focusing a selector; this can type into or submit the current page, delivering agent-supplied keystrokes or previously filled data to an attacker-controlled page.

playwright_save_as_pdf.rationale: Saves the current page as a local PDF (`Save the current page as a PDF file`) under `outputPath`/`filename`; the description does not advertise returning the page content or sending it to an attacker-readable destination.

playwright_click_and_switch_tab.rationale: Clicks a link and switches tabs (`Click a link and switch to the newly opened tab`); the click can trigger navigation/submission from attacker-controlled page content and can send agent-supplied page state.

notes: No tool is advertised as disabled by default, so all default_enabled values are true.
`playwright_evaluate` is treated as browser-page JavaScript execution, not HOSTEXEC, because the advertised text says `in the browser console` and does not advertise arbitrary host code execution.
